h1: Milling machines — turret, universal and drilling-milling machines
intro: Milling machines cut flat faces, slots, steps, pockets and keyways with rotating cutters while the table moves the work under them. NovoTech's value-line milling machines are built in China to our specification: knee-type turret mills with a horizontal spindle as well as the vertical head, universal mills with a head that swivels through 360°, heavy ISO50 universal mills with power feed and rapid traverse on all axes and tables up to 79″, drilling-milling machines that drill 2″, a mini mill-drill and a radial drill-mill, and a keyseater and a slotting machine for keyways and splines. Parts and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Turret mill, universal mill or drill-mill?
faq.a: A turret (Bridgeport-type) mill has a vertical head that tilts and a knee that moves the table up and down — the most flexible machine for one-off parts, slots and pockets. A universal mill adds a horizontal spindle and arbor for side and slab milling and gang cutters, and swivels its head through 360°. A drill-mill drills and mills on one column without a knee: the lower-cost choice when most of the work is drilling with some face milling.

faq.q: What do ISO40 and ISO50 mean?
faq.a: They are the sizes of the spindle taper that holds the tool holder: ISO40 (NT40, the same size as CAT40 and BT40) for general milling, ISO50 for heavier cuts and larger face mills. R8 and MT tapers are found on small mills. Tell us what tooling you already have — adapters are available.

Power feed moves the table at a steady rate for a better finish and less operator fatigue; a digital readout (DRO) shows the table position to 0.0002″ and replaces the dials for most work. The X6336 and LM-1450 have power feed on all three axes; DROs are available on most models — ask us when you quote.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
